question: Standard pulse oximetry (SpO₂) reliably monitors oxygen saturation in carbon monoxide poisoning and accurately reflects the degree of CO intoxication.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Standard pulse oximetry gives a falsely normal reading because HbCO absorbs light at similar wavelengths to HbO₂. Only co-oximetry (multi-wavelength spectrophotometry) can specifically measure HbCO. A 'normal' SpO₂ in a patient from an enclosed space should never rule out CO poisoning.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Standard two-wavelength pulse oximeters cannot distinguish carboxyhaemoglobin (HbCO) from oxyhaemoglobin (HbO₂). SpO₂ reads falsely NORMAL (or even elevated) in severe CO poisoning. Co-oximetry is required to measure actual HbCO levels.
